title: 2006 AMC 12B Problem 14
statement: Elmo makes \(N\) sandwiches for a fundraiser. For each sandwich he uses \(B\) globs of peanut butter at \(4\)¢ per glob and \(J\) blobs of jam at \(5\)¢ per blob. The cost of the peanut butter and jam to make all the sandwiches is \(\$2.53.\) Assume that \(B,\) \(J,\) and \(N\) are positive integers with \(N \gt 1.\) What is the cost of the jam Elmo uses to make the sandwiches?

solutions.text:
The total cost in cents is \(N(4B + 5J) = 253 = 11 \cdot 23.\) Since \(N \gt 1,\) the value of \(N\) is \(11,\) \(23,\) or \(253.\)

If \(N = 253\) then \(4B + 5J = 1,\) and if \(N = 23\) then \(4B + 5J = 11;\) neither has a positive integer solution.

So \(N = 11\) and \(4B + 5J = 23,\) whose only positive solution is \(B = 2,\) \(J = 3.\)

The jam costs \(N \cdot J \cdot 5\)¢ \(= 11 \cdot 3 \cdot 5 = 165\) cents, or \(\$1.65.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: The total cost is \(N(4B + 5J) = 253\) cents; factor \(253\)
Test \(N = 11, 23, 253,\) then determine the numbers of peanut-butter globs \(B\) and jam blobs \(J\)
